rule: Each player takes seven tiles. The player with the double six plays first in a match.
quote: the first person to play is the person who has the double six

rule: After the first hand, the winner of the hand leads the next one and may open with any tile.
quote: the person who wins the hand, or “mano,” who will be the leader

rule: Play goes to the right of the player who just played (counter-clockwise). A player who cannot match either end loses his turn.
quote: the game is played in a counter-clockwise fashion

rule: Doubles are placed crosswise, and players may not play off the sides of doubles; play is only on the two open ends.
quote: players are not allowed to play off of the doubles on the table

rule: The double six opens the first game. Later games are opened by the winner of the previous game, and the next tile is played by the player to his right.
quote: Las demás partidas las inicia quien haya ganado la partida anterior.

rule: Dominican game: two teams of 1 or 2 players each. In 1v1, each player takes 7 tiles, and the rest stay in the pile to draw from when unable to play.
quote: En la modalidad de 1 jugador por equipo, los jugadores toman 7 fichas cada uno

rule: 1v1 variant: each player takes ten tiles, and drawing from the pile is not allowed.
quote: ambos jugadores toma diez fichas y no es permitido “cargar” de la pila

rule: Passing with a playable tile: all points after that pass go to the opponents. If the player corrects it before the next player plays, the penalty is 25 or 30.
quote: solo recibirá una sanción de 25 o 30 puntos dependiendo de las reglas

rule: With four players, each takes seven tiles.
quote: Cuando juegan cuatro personas, cada jugador toma siete fichas.

rule: The player who places the first tile is the 'mano' for that hand.
quote: El jugador que coloca la primera ficha es “mano” en esa partida.

rule: Later games are started by the winner of the previous game.
quote: las subsiguientes son iniciadas por el ganador de la partida anterior

rule: Santiago tournament: the first lead is with the double six, and later leads rotate (not winner-leads). A player may ask about the lead (rule 10).
quote: SALIDA ROTATIVA.
sourceName: Momento Deportivo RD, Copa Alcaldía de Santiago rules (2019)

rule: Santiago tournament: passing with a playable tile (also a mis-matched tile, 'chivo') costs 100 in total: minus 50 for the offending pair and plus 50 for the other pair. Then the tiles are reshuffled.
quote: PASO CON FICHA SON 100 PUNTOS, MENOS 50 PARA LA PAREJA INFRACTORA
sourceName: Momento Deportivo RD, Copa Alcaldía de Santiago rules (2019)

rule: La Guáyiga tournament: passing while holding a playable tile gives +30 to the other team.
quote: Si pasas con fichas: +30 pts al equipo contrario.
sourceName: Junta del Distrito Municipal La Guáyiga (2025)

rule: Forum answer from a DR resident: the game starts with the double six and goes anticlockwise, with partners sitting across.
quote: the game starts by playing the double six, then continues in an anticlockwise fashion

rule: FichaFlow: in the standard 2v2, all 28 tiles are dealt, 7 each, with no boneyard. A player must play when able and cannot choose to pass.
quote: You cannot choose to pass when you have a legal tile.

rule: FichaFlow: in 1v1 and 3-player games, each player gets 7 tiles and the rest go to a face-down boneyard.
quote: each player still gets seven tiles and the remaining tiles go face-down to the boneyard

rule: FichaFlow: after the first hand, many tables let the previous winner keep the lead.
quote: many tables let the previous winner keep la mano and start again

rule: The double six orders the start: holding it means you lead.
quote: el doble seis. Tenerlo es salir, marcar el primer paso
sourceName: El Inmobiliario, 'La tradición del dominó: Porque aquí no se pasa con fichas'

rule: Generic Spanish rule: passing is not allowed with a playable tile. After the first game, the lead rotates to the right with a free choice of tile.
quote: No se permitirá el pase teniendo opción de juego

rule: FID: every player takes 7 tiles. The opener takes first, then the players to his right, which means play and dealing go to the right (counterclockwise).
quote: en segundo y tercer lugar, los situados a la derecha de éste
sourceName: Federación Internacional de Dominó, Reglamento de Juego (2015, Art. 74c)

rule: FID: the first opener of a match is chosen by each player drawing a tile. The highest tile opens, not the double six.
quote: Corresponderá salir a aquél que presente la de puntuación más alta
sourceName: Federación Internacional de Dominó, Reglamento de Juego (2015, Art. 74b)

rule: FID 2024: the next hand is opened by the player to the right of the previous hand's opener (rotation), not by the winner.
quote: La próxima mano sale el atleta a la derecha o trasmano de la mano anterior
sourceName: Federación Internacional de Dominó, Reglamento (2024 edition, Art. 76)

rule: FID: saying 'paso' while holding a playable tile gives a yellow card and a 40% deduction of the target. If it prevents a tranca or domination, it gives a red card and loss of the match.
quote: pronuncie la palabra paso teniendo fichas por jugar
sourceName: Federación Internacional de Dominó, Reglamento de Juego (2015, Art. 81)

rule: FEMUNDO: the first opener is chosen by lot and the opener then rotates. The shuffler is the player to the left of the opener.
quote: La primera salida será sorteada y luego será rotada.

rule: FEMUNDO: each player plays with 7 tiles.
quote: Se juega con 7 fichas por atleta.

rule: Dominican game: the holder of the double six opens the first game.
quote: el jugador que posee el seis doble realiza la salida de la primera partida

rule: Dominican game: the winner of the previous hand opens later hands. The next tile is played by the player to the opener's right.
quote: Las demás partidas las inicia quien haya ganado la partida anterior.

rule: Dominican game: play passes to the player on the right.
quote: La próxima ficha la coloca el jugador a la derecha de este.

rule: Dominican game: sides are teams of 1 or 2 players, so 1v1 and 2v2 are both recognized.
quote: Dos equipos de 1 o 2 jugadores cada uno.

rule: Dominican 1v1 ('Pila'): each player takes 7 tiles and the rest go to a pile. A player who cannot play draws from the pile one tile at a time until he finds a playable one.
quote: toman 7 fichas cada uno, quedando las fichas restantes a un lado

rule: Dominican 1v1 variant: each player takes ten tiles and drawing from the pile is not allowed.
quote: ambos jugadores toma diez fichas y no es permitido “cargar” de la pila

rule: Each player takes 7 tiles. The holder of the double six plays first in a match.
quote: the first person to play is the person who has the double six

rule: After the first hand, the winner of the hand leads the next one and may open with any tile.
quote: can play any fichas he or she desires

rule: Play goes to the right of the player who just played (counterclockwise). A player with no matching tile passes.
quote: the game is played in a counter-clockwise fashion

rule: Doubles are placed crosswise, and players may not play off the sides of doubles. Only the two open ends of the line are playable, so there are no spinners.
quote: players are not allowed to play off of the doubles on the table

rule: Santiago 2019 tournament: the double six opens (rule 1) and the opener rotates (rule 2).
quote: SALIDA CON DOBLE SEIS.
sourceName: Momento Deportivo RD, Copa Alcaldía de Santiago rules (2019)

rule: La Guáyiga 2025 tournament: a lifted tile must be played, and passing with a playable tile gives +30 to the opposing team.
quote: Si levantas ficha y vas, debes jugarla.
sourceName: Junta del Distrito Municipal La Guáyiga, tournament rules (2025)

rule: When four people play, each player takes seven tiles. The player who places the first tile is the 'mano'.
quote: Cuando juegan cuatro personas, cada jugador toma siete fichas.

rule: Generic: passing is not allowed when the player has a tile that fits either end, whether or not the play is convenient.
quote: No se permitirá el pase teniendo opción de juego
sourceName: Dominó, arte o ciencia: Reglas del Dominó

rule: App: in 1v1 and 3-player games each player gets 7 tiles and the rest go to a boneyard. The standard 2v2 game deals all 28 tiles.
quote: 1v1 and 3-player formats deal seven tiles each — the rest go to the boneyard.

rule: App: a player cannot choose to pass while holding a legal tile.
quote: You cannot choose to pass when you have a legal tile.

rule: App: the highest double leads the first hand. After that, the partnership that won the previous hand opens with any tile.
quote: the player whose frente won the previous hand opens the next one

rule: Puerto Rico: the double six opens the first game. In 2- or 3-player games where nobody drew the double six, the highest double opens. The winner of the previous game opens later games with any tile, and play goes counterclockwise.
quote: if the double 6 wasn't drawn, then the highest double starts the game
sourceName: José Carrillo, 'Domino Games in Puerto Rico' (archived)

rule: USA Domino Federation: falsely saying 'paso' while holding playable tiles gives a -25 point fine to the offender.
quote: Si un jugador FALSAMENTE dice PASO, y tiene fichas para jugar, conlleva multa

rule: Team play: each player takes seven tiles. The holder of the double six plays first in a match.
quote: in a match the first person to play is the person who has the double six

rule: After the first hand, the winner of the previous hand leads the next one and may lead with any tile.
quote: can play any fichas he or she desires

rule: The next player is the one to the right; play goes counter-clockwise. A player with no matching tile forfeits the turn.
quote: the game is played in a counter-clockwise fashion

rule: Doubles are laid crosswise and no play is allowed off the sides of a double; only the two open ends are playable.
quote: players are not allowed to play off of the doubles on the table

rule: The double-six holder opens the first game. Later games are opened by the winner of the previous game, and the next tile is placed by the player to the right.
quote: Las demás partidas las inicia quien haya ganado la partida anterior.

rule: Dominican 1v1 (one player per team): 7 tiles each, the rest in a pile. A player who cannot play draws one at a time until a playable tile appears.
quote: debe “cargar” fichas de la pila, una por una hasta encontrar aquella

rule: La Mesa: the opening does not rotate; the team that won the previous hand opens. The double six opens the first hand.
quote: la salida no rota: la sale el equipo que ganó la mano anterior
sourceName: La Mesa: Dominó Latino, Reglas del dominó dominicano

rule: La Mesa states turns go clockwise, which contradicts DR1, Wikipedia, FichaFlow and OurPastimes (counter-clockwise, to the right).
quote: Se juega por turnos en el sentido de las manecillas del reloj.
sourceName: La Mesa: Dominó Latino, Reglas del dominó dominicano

rule: La Mesa: a player must play when able; passing is allowed only with no playable tile.
quote: Jugar es obligatorio: si tienes una ficha que pegue, tienes que ponerla.
sourceName: La Mesa: Dominó Latino, Reglas del dominó dominicano

rule: La Mesa: if a hand must be redealt, the same player who opened opens again.
quote: hay que repartir de nuevo, vuelve a salir quien salió
sourceName: La Mesa: Dominó Latino, Reglas del dominó dominicano

rule: FichaFlow: the four-player game deals all 28 tiles with no boneyard. 1v1 and 3-player games deal seven each, and the rest go to a boneyard.
quote: The game is also played 1v1 or with three players — those formats use a boneyard
sourceName: FichaFlow, How to Play Dominican Domino

rule: FichaFlow: play moves counter-clockwise and a player must play if able; you cannot choose to pass with a legal tile.
quote: Play moves counter-clockwise. If you can answer one of the open ends, you must play.
sourceName: FichaFlow, How to Play Dominican Domino

rule: FichaFlow: the most common rule is that the team that won the previous hand keeps 'la mano' and opens with any tile. The 6-6 requirement applies only to the first hand.
quote: the team that won the previous hand keeps la mano
sourceName: FichaFlow, Who Goes First in Dominican Domino

rule: FichaFlow variant: some tables rotate the opening one seat to the right each hand, whoever won.
quote: Some tables rotate instead, passing the start one seat to the right each hand
sourceName: FichaFlow, Who Goes First in Dominican Domino

rule: Boarden: in the first hand the holder of the highest double leads with it. Later hands are led by the winning team's player, with any tile.
quote: whoever holds the highest double must lead with it
sourceName: Boarden, How to play Dominican dominoes

rule: Santiago tournament (2019): the first opening is with the double six, and after that the opening rotates.
quote: SALIDA ROTATIVA.
sourceName: Momento Deportivo RD, Reglas del torneo Copa Alcaldía de Santiago 2019

rule: Tranca (open-source Dominican game): the first hand has a forced double-six opening. Later hands are opened by the last player who played in the previous hand.
quote: Deal the next hand; the previous hand's last player to play opens.

rule: DR1 forum poster: the four-person partner game starts with the double six and continues anticlockwise.
quote: the game starts by playing the double six, then continues in an anticlockwise fashion

rule: OurPastimes: turns rotate counter-clockwise; each player draws seven.
quote: Rotate turns counter-clockwise
sourceName: OurPastimes, How to Play Dominican Dominoes

rule: GameVelvet Dominó Mano a Mano (generic 1v1): 7 tiles each and 14 in a draw pool. Draw until you can play, and pass only when the pool is empty. The highest double starts; game to 100.
quote: 7 tiles each player. 14 bones at the draw pool.
sourceName: GameVelvet, How to Play Dominó Mano a Mano

rule: Dominó en Parejas (Spanish app, generic rules): later rounds are opened by the player to the right, with any tile; target typically 100.
quote: En las rondas siguientes el turno pasa al jugador de la derecha
sourceName: Dominó en Parejas by Producciones Don Naipe (App Store listing)

rule: Mesa28 (Puerto Rico): later hands are opened by the previous hand's winner, except after a tied tranca.
quote: En las manos siguientes sale quien ganó la mano anterior, salvo una tranca empatada.

rule: The holder of the double six opens the first game; later games are opened by the winner of the previous one; the next tile is played by the player to the right.
quote: el jugador que posee el seis doble realiza la salida de la primera partida

rule: Later hands are opened by whoever won the previous one.
quote: Las demás partidas las inicia quien haya ganado la partida anterior.

rule: Play goes to the right of the opener (counterclockwise).
quote: La próxima ficha la coloca el jugador a la derecha de este.

rule: 1v1 (one player per team): 7 tiles each, the rest in the pila; a player who cannot play draws one by one until he finds a playable tile. A variant deals 10 each with no drawing.
quote: una por una hasta encontrar aquella que pueda ser colocada

rule: 1v1 variant: both players take ten tiles and drawing from the pile is not allowed.
quote: ambos jugadores toma diez fichas y no es permitido

rule: Four-player game: partners sit across; the game starts with the double six and goes anticlockwise.
quote: the game starts by playing the double six, then continues in an anticlockwise fashion
sourceName: DR1.com forum, Rules for Dominican Dominoes?, user The Gorgon, 2013

rule: Forum (2009): 7 tiles each; highest double opens; each new round is started by the previous round's winner (either partner may start). This post says play passes to the left, which conflicts with other sources.
quote: Each new round is started by winner of previous round
sourceName: DR1.com forum, Rules for playing domino, user Mega_Man, 2009

rule: Santiago tournament (2019): opening with the double six, and the opener rotates each hand.
quote: SALIDA CON DOBLE SEIS
sourceName: Momento Deportivo RD, 1er Torneo de Dominó Copa Alcaldía de Santiago reglamento (2019)

rule: Santiago tournament (2019): the salida is rotative (not kept by the winner).
quote: SALIDA ROTATIVA
sourceName: Momento Deportivo RD, 1er Torneo de Dominó Copa Alcaldía de Santiago reglamento (2019)

rule: FichaFlow: first hand opens with the 6-6; later the winning team keeps la mano and opens with any tile; some tables rotate the start one seat to the right instead.
quote: its player opens the next hand with any tile they choose
sourceName: FichaFlow, Who Goes First? La Salida

rule: FichaFlow: 2v2 deals all 28 tiles (7 each, no boneyard); in 1v1 or 3-player each gets 7 and the rest stays in the boneyard.
quote: each player gets seven tiles and the remaining tiles stay face-down in the boneyard
sourceName: FichaFlow, How to Play Dominican Domino

rule: FichaFlow: a pass is legal only when you cannot answer either end; if you hold a legal tile you must play it.
quote: If you hold a legal response, you must play it.
sourceName: FichaFlow, Dominican Domino Passing Rules Explained

rule: Dominican-labeled game sheet: the holder of double-six opens, failing that double-five and so on; a player who can play must play, otherwise knocks.
quote: holding the double-six, or failing that the double-five and so on
sourceName: International Game Descriptions PDF, Dominoes (Dominican Republic)

rule: General rules: passing is not allowed while holding a playable tile; play is counterclockwise; after the first hand the salida rotates and the opener picks any tile.
quote: No se permitirá el pase teniendo opción de juego
sourceName: Dominó: arte o ciencia, Reglas del Dominó

rule: FID: the first opener is chosen by drawing tiles; each player takes 7; the next hand is opened by the player to the right of the previous opener.
quote: La próxima mano sale el atleta a la derecha o trasmano de la mano anterior.
sourceName: Federación Internacional de Dominó, Reglamento (2024), Arts. 74, 76

rule: Puerto Rico: in 2- or 3-player games, if nobody drew the double six, the highest double opens; players draw from the boneyard until they can play.
quote: if the double 6 wasn't drawn, then the highest double starts the game
sourceName: Caribbean Trading, The Basics of Puerto Rican Dominoes Rules

rule: Generic mano a mano (online game): 7 tiles each, 14 in the draw pile; the highest double opens; draw until a tile fits; game to 50.
quote: El jugador que comienza la partida es el que tiene el doble más alto
sourceName: Magnojuegos, Dominó Mano a Mano reglas

rule: Generic partnership rules: players must play if they legally can; play is normally counterclockwise; 6-6 holder leads the first deal.
quote: Players must play a tile at their turn if they legally can.

rule: Teams are 1 or 2 players each (1v1 or 2v2).
quote: Dos equipos de 1 o 2 jugadores cada uno.

rule: The holder of the double six opens the first game.
quote: el jugador que posee el seis doble realiza la salida de la primera partida

rule: Later hands are opened by whoever won the previous hand.
quote: Las demás partidas las inicia quien haya ganado la partida anterior.

rule: Play passes to the player on the right of the opener.
quote: La próxima ficha la coloca el jugador a la derecha de este.

rule: A player of the losing team shuffles.
quote: Un jugador del equipo perdedor le tocara barajar las fichas.

rule: 1v1: each player takes 7 tiles, the rest form the pila; a player who cannot play draws one by one until he can play.
quote: debe “cargar” fichas de la pila, una por una

rule: 1v1 variant: each player takes ten tiles and drawing from the pila is not allowed.
quote: ambos jugadores toma diez fichas y no es permitido “cargar” de la pila

rule: Passing while holding a playable tile: all points after that pass are counted for the opponents (or a 25/30 penalty if corrected in time).
quote: los puntos de todas las fichas después de ese pase se cuentan a los oponentes
sourceName: Wikipedia (es), Dominó, section Dominó dominicano (Pase con ficha)

rule: DR1: the double six opens the first game of a match.
quote: the first person to play is the person who has the double six
sourceName: DR1.com, 25, 50, Capicua! Dominoes and the Dominican Republic (page 1, archived)

rule: DR1: the winner of the hand leads the next game and may play any tile.
quote: the person who wins the hand, or “mano,” who will be the leader
sourceName: DR1.com, 25, 50, Capicua! Dominoes and the Dominican Republic (page 1, archived)

rule: DR1: play goes counter-clockwise.
quote: the game is played in a counter-clockwise fashion
sourceName: DR1.com, 25, 50, Capicua! Dominoes and the Dominican Republic (page 1, archived)

rule: DR1: doubles are placed crosswise and nobody may play off the sides of a double (only two open ends).
quote: players are not allowed to play off of the doubles on the table
sourceName: DR1.com, 25, 50, Capicua! Dominoes and the Dominican Republic (page 1, archived)

rule: Santiago 2019 tournament: the game opens with the double six.
quote: SALIDA CON DOBLE SEIS.
sourceName: Momento Deportivo RD, Reglas del torneo de dominó Copa Alcaldía de Santiago (Aug 2019)

rule: Santiago 2019 tournament: after a penalty or tie the next opener follows the rotation (rotating salida in that event).
quote: SALE QUIEN LE TOCA SALIR EN LA ROTACION
sourceName: Momento Deportivo RD, Reglas del torneo de dominó Copa Alcaldía de Santiago (Aug 2019)

rule: Santiago 2019 tournament: a hand with five doubles is still played (no redeal).
quote: CINCO BOBLE SE JUEGA.
sourceName: Momento Deportivo RD, Reglas del torneo de dominó Copa Alcaldía de Santiago (Aug 2019)

rule: La Guayiga 2025 tournament: tiles are only reshuffled if a player gets all 7 doubles.
quote: Solo se baraja si salen los 7 dobles.
sourceName: Junta del Distrito Municipal La Guáyiga, Gran Torneo de Dominó Regular 3/2 (Oct 2025)

rule: La Guayiga 2025 tournament: passing while holding a playable tile gives 30 points to the other team.
quote: Si pasas con fichas: +30 pts al equipo contrario.
sourceName: Junta del Distrito Municipal La Guáyiga, Gran Torneo de Dominó Regular 3/2 (Oct 2025)

rule: Dominican style: the team in the lead keeps the opening; the starter is not rotated.
quote: The team in the lead does not give up position

rule: FichaFlow: play is counter-clockwise and a player must play if he can answer an open end.
quote: Play moves counter-clockwise. If you can answer one of the open ends, you must play.
sourceName: FichaFlow, How to Play Dominican Domino

rule: FichaFlow: in 1v1 and 3-player games each player gets seven tiles and the rest go to a boneyard.
quote: each player still gets seven tiles and the remaining tiles go face-down to the boneyard
sourceName: FichaFlow, How to Play Dominican Domino

rule: FichaFlow: from hand two, most commonly a player of the winning team opens with any tile; some tables rotate the opener one seat to the right.
quote: passing the start one seat to the right each hand regardless of who won
sourceName: FichaFlow, Who Goes First? La Salida

rule: Boarden: the team that won the previous hand opens the next one with any tile.
quote: the player whose frente won the previous hand opens the next one
sourceName: Boarden, How to play Dominican dominoes

rule: Puerto Rico: in 2 or 3 player games, if nobody drew the double six, the highest double starts.
quote: if the double 6 wasn't drawn, then the highest double starts the game
sourceName: José Carrillo, Jose's Page on Domino Games in Puerto Rico (archived)

rule: USA Domino Federation: the opening rotates.
quote: La SALIDA es ROTATIVA.

rule: Low-reliability site says Dominican play goes clockwise (contradicts all other Dominican sources).
quote: O jogo avança no sentido horário
